- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in early days of the 30-day window.
- Forecasts tend to be too low in the first 5–10 days, then gradually rise — suggesting a lag in capturing near-term price momentum.
- After sharp spikes in history (e.g., 80+), model forecasts overshoot and then correct — indicating overreaction to recent highs.
- Mean reversion is not fully captured: model often fails to anticipate sharp downward corrections after peaks.
- Forecasts show persistent downward bias in the latter half of the 30-day window, suggesting underestimation of price stability or volatility decay.
- Model exhibits poor sensitivity to recent history when history is trending upward — underestimates continuation or reversal.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in the early part of the window, especially when history is trending up — fails to capture momentum.
- Model tends to overcorrect after minor price drops, leading to premature recovery forecasts.
